III Do you know if these spices can be used for something else other than cooking? Let us find out by reading the letter given below.

Dear Vikram and Vaibhavi,
Namaste! I just got your message that you are better now.
I am happy that the natural cures that I had shared, helped you. You should
try to remember these cures and may share them with your friends. When
I was a child, I learnt them from my grandmother. She used to find home
remedies for most of the weather-related common illnesses. Let me share
some of the benefits of the spices that most of us have in our kitchen.
Let me start with haldi, which is called turmeric in English. It helps in improving
our energy level and digestion. It helps in reducing body pain too.
Next, let us take methi, which is called fenugreek in English. You will be
surprised to know that it helps me in keeping my sugar level and my body
weight in control. I need to soak the methi seeds overnight and drink the water
in the morning.
• Jeera (cumin) seeds soaked in water overnight can also improve digestion and
help cure sleeplessness.
• You know, when you were babies and had gas in your tummy, I used to put
heeng (asafoetida) water on your tummy to give you some relief. Heeng
can also help in controlling cough and cold.
• Dalchini (cinnamon) and laung (clove) give relief when we have toothache
till we can consult a dentist.
• Adrak (ginger) is another herb that can help us when we have cough and
cold. It also gives relief from pain. Do you know, ginger has been used in
cooking for more than 4000 years? Even today, it is extensively used in
cooking Indian food.
• Kali mirch (black pepper) is also helpful in digestion and can give us relief
from body pain.
• You may have seen that at the end of a meal, saunf (fennel seeds) and
ajwain (carom seeds) are served. It is because they help in the digestion of
food.
• Elaichi (cardamom) also helps us with digestion and respiratory troubles
in addition to curing bad breath.

Definition of Spices

A spice is any seed, fruit, root, bark, leaf or any other part of a plant used to give taste and colour to our food.

Examples of Spices

Examples of spices include turmeric, fenugreek, cumin seeds, asafoetida, cinnamon, clove, ginger, black pepper, fennel seeds, cardamom.

Benefits of Turmeric (Haldi)

Turmeric helps in improving energy level and digestion, reduces body pain, and is known as haldi.

Benefits of Fenugreek (Methi)

Fenugreek helps in keeping sugar level and body weight in control. It can also help manage cough and cold.

Benefits of Cumin Seeds (Jeera)

Cumin seeds soaked in water overnight can improve digestion and help cure sleeplessness.

Benefits of Asafoetida (Heeng)

Asafoetida can help control cough and cold. It is used to give relief from gas in the tummy.

Benefits of Cinnamon (Dalchini)

Cinnamon gives relief when we have toothache until we can consult a dentist.

Benefits of Clove (Laung)

Clove gives relief when we have toothache until we can consult a dentist.

Benefits of Ginger (Adrak)

Ginger helps us when we have cough and cold. It also gives relief from pain and is used in cooking for more than 4000 years.

Benefits of Black Pepper (Kali mirch)

Black pepper is helpful in digestion and can give us relief from body pain.

Benefits of Fennel Seeds (Saunf)

Fennel seeds help in the digestion of food when served at the end of a meal.

Benefits of Cardamom (Elaichi)

Cardamom helps with digestion and respiratory troubles, and cures bad breath.
